title: Modules (Part 1) - Public API boundaries
learning_objectives: Group related helper functions inside an inline module.
Expose a supported public API while keeping implementation helpers private.
Import a public function with `use` and call it through a stable path.
explanation: This slice focuses on modules as an API boundary tool. The learner practices keeping a helper private, exposing one public function, and then consuming that public function through an imported path.

examples.title: Keep the helper private and expose one function
Call the public API through its full path
Import the public API with `use`
examples.code:
use crate::text_tools::word_count;

let count = word_count("hello Rust");

completion_criteria: Exercise tests pass through the public API without exposing the helper
Learner can distinguish the helper's internal definition path from the exported access path
Learner can explain why a private helper can still support a public module API
